title: Present Perfect: Uso, Conjugação de Verbos Irregulares e Vocabulário Essencial

Sarah's hair was long. Now it is very short.Sarah has cut her hair.2. The floor was dirty. Now it is clean.The floor has been cleaned. – O chão foi limpo (by my sister)My sister has cleaned the floor. – Minha irmã limpou o chão.3. Mark's car isn’t in his garage. He is walking to work.Mark has sold his car. 4. The oven is warm and there is a cake on the table.My mother has cooked /baked a cake.5. They are standing outside because they don't have their keys.They have lost their keys.6. The ground is wet and there are puddles everywhere.It has rained.7. I am not hungry anymore. My plate is empty.I have eaten all the food. I have had lunch. 8. The TV is off and the room is quiet.My dad has slept. My dad has gone to bed.My dad has gone to sleep. 9. James has a bandage on his finger and he's in pain.James has cut his finger.James has hurt his finger.10. The email is in the draft box. Present perfect: I haven’t finished it yet.Present simple: I don’t finish any email I start. Past simple: I didn’t finish the email yesterday.11. I don't see my phone anywhere on the desk.Present perfect: It has been taken to a service shop / a technician / a repair shop.                It has been lost. Present simple: I always lose my cell phone.Past simple: I lost my cell phone yesterday.12. Her computer is off and she isn’t at her office desk. Present perfect: She had gone home.Present continuous: She is driving now.Present simple: She is happy.Past simple: She went away after class.13. The window is broken and there is a ball on the floor.14. People are leaving the cinema.15. I know this author. He’s very good.

enriched.summary: The class focuses on the Present Perfect tense, emphasizing its connection to the present and how it is used to describe completed actions with relevance to the current moment. It also includes vocabulary building with translations, examples, pronunciation, and irregular verb conjugations.

vocabulary.definition: An enclosed compartment for heating, baking, or roasting food.
examples: The oven is warm and there is a cake on the table.

vocabulary.definition: To cook food by dry heat, usually in an oven.
examples: My mother has baked a cake.

vocabulary.definition: To no longer have something because you do not know where it is.
examples: I always lose my cell phone.

vocabulary.definition: The past and past participle form of 'lose'.
examples: I lost my cell phone yesterday.

vocabulary.definition: A small pool of liquid, especially rainwater, on the ground.
examples: The ground is wet and there are puddles everywhere.

vocabulary.definition: A breed of dog known for its curly coat.
examples: I saw a poodle at the park.

vocabulary.definition: To put food into your mouth and swallow it.
examples: I have eaten all the food.
I have eaten all the food.

vocabulary.definition: To cause physical pain or injury.
To eat a meal in the middle of the day.

grammar.explanation: The Present Perfect is used to describe actions that happened at an unspecified time in the past and are connected to the present.
rules: Use for actions with relevance to the present moment.
commonMistakes: Using the past simple instead of the present perfect.
Forgetting to use the past participle form of the verb.

practiceQuestions.question: Transform the sentence into Present Perfect: 'Lisa charged her phone.'
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Present Perfect is formed with 'has' + past participle.

practiceQuestions.question: Choose the correct form: 'They (have lost / lost) their keys.'
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Present Perfect is used to indicate a past action with relevance to the present.

culturalNotes: In English-speaking countries, Present Perfect is often used to indicate achievements or completed tasks relevant to the present.
The use of Present Perfect can vary between American and British English, with British English favoring it more frequently.
studyTips: Pay attention to the context to decide between Present Perfect and Past Simple.
Use flashcards to memorize vocabulary and their past participle forms.
originalExamples: Lisa’s phone battery was at 35%, but now it’s at 100%. (A bateria do celular da Lisa estava em 35%, mas agora está em 100%.)
Sarah's hair was long. Now it is very short. (O cabelo da Sarah era comprido. Agora está muito curto.)
The floor was dirty. Now it is clean. (O chão estava sujo. Agora está limpo.)
Mark's car isn’t in his garage. He is walking to work. (O carro do Mark não está na garagem. Ele está andando para o trabalho.)
The oven is warm and there is a cake on the table. (O forno está quente e há um bolo na mesa.)
They are standing outside because they don't have their keys. (Eles estão do lado de fora porque não têm as chaves.)
The ground is wet and there are puddles everywhere. (O chão está molhado e há poças por toda parte.)
I am not hungry anymore. My plate is empty. (Eu não estou mais com fome. Meu prato está vazio.)
The TV is off and the room is quiet. (A TV está desligada e a sala está silenciosa.)
James has a bandage on his finger and he's in pain. (James tem um curativo no dedo e está com dor.)
The email is in the draft box. (O e-mail está na caixa de rascunhos.)
I don't see my phone anywhere on the desk. (Não vejo meu celular em nenhum lugar na mesa.)
Her computer is off and she isn’t at her office desk. (O computador dela está desligado e ela não está na mesa do escritório.)
The window is broken and there is a ball on the floor. (A janela está quebrada e há uma bola no chão.)
People are leaving the cinema. (As pessoas estão saindo do cinema.)
I know this author. He’s very good. (Eu conheço este autor. Ele é muito bom.)
